text:
anya_ml: FYI saw a 30% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for model rdx-13b on Private in EU after the weekend deploy. root cause unclear, filing here before digging in.

maria_ops: any error spikes? logs?

anya_ml: latency p50 for token generation up ~120ms, token cost up. Prom profiler shows KV GET latency jump from ~0.8ms -> ~15ms for private nodes.

jon_sre: do we use network-backed KV (NFS/redis) for Private? that could explain it.

anya_ml: yes, Private is hitting customer-managed redis placed in VPC. Dedicated/Hosted use local in-process cache. But weirdly hit-rate also dropped (from 78% -> 55%) not just latency.

dave_platform: could be keying change? we recently normalized prompt templates in runtime @last-week; maybe session id or prefix trimming changed.

anya_ml: I compared keys pre/post: looks like we started including the ephemeral request_id in the normalized key for ~2% of requests due to upstream middleware adding trace header. So collisions are actually increases in cardinality -> lower hit-rate.

jon_sre: can you paste the snippet that generates keys?

anya_ml: ```
// simplified
function makeCacheKey(model, prompt, session) {
  const normalized = normalizePrompt(prompt); // trims whitespace, lowercases
  return `${model}::${session.id}::${hash(normalized)}`;
}
```

maria_ops: ah, session.id sometimes contains request_id in Private because of proxy rewrite. That would blow up cardinality.

dave_platform: two things: 1) revert to using stable session.user_id for Private? 2) add a fast client-side dedupe before hitting redis.

anya_ml: also noticed our warmup job is aggressive for Private: it prefetches top-10 prefixes per session across 100k sessions which explodes egress to customer redis and saturates replication lag -> higher GET latency -> timeouts -> cache misses.

jon_sre: that explains interplay: keying increases cardinality so warmup becomes noisy and backfills, flooding the network-backed store.

maria_ops: workaround deployed: reduced warmup fanout from 10->2 for Private and added a backoff. early results: GET latency down to ~3.5ms and hit-rate recovered to ~68% within 12m.

anya_ml: perf regression root cause: key normalization + warmup fanout + network-backed KV. Hosted/Dedicated unaffected because they use local caches and don't do cross-VPC egress.

dave_platform: long term: 1) enforce keying contract in runtime (no request-id). 2) telemetry: add cache_key_entropy metric and per-store QPS/latency alert. 3) make warmup topology-aware (avoid prefetching for sessions mapped to external KV)

jon_sre: can we add a hard guard in Private config: when KV backend is remote, cap warmup concurrency and optionally switch to passive warmup?

maria_ops: adding a config flag now: private.warmup.mode = passive|aggressive. Set to passive for all VPCs by default until we ship safeguards.

anya_ml: filed infra ticket INF-4098 to add key-contract lint and warning in build. Also PR up to revert session.id -> user_id in runtime: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rdx-runtime/pull/1423

dave_platform: yay. also note: kernel selection/batching still matter — we saw more small requests post-miss which degrade batching efficiency. So this is cascading.

jon_sre: good catch. can we add a synthetic test that simulates high-cardinality keys against a redis to measure warmup impact?

anya_ml: yes, I'll sketch a load test harness and share results tomorrow. thanks all :rocket: 

deploy-bot: Deployed config private.warmup.mode=passive to eu-private-cluster (rollout 20%).

maria_ops: monitoring looks stable. closing this thread for now. :white_check_mark:
